- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect recent low as baseline.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mid-term (days 10–20) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; reduce forecast by 1–2% in those intervals.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
